newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Globus says H1 op profit down, exports up.
newsitem.headline: Globus says H1 op profit down, exports up.

text.p: Hungarian tinned food manufacturer Globus Konzervipari Rt said on Monday its operating profit in the first half of 1997 fell from last year, but its after-tax profit was in line with its plans.

"The company did not fully build in raw material prices in its sales prices in order to maintain its market, therefore the operating profit remained below last year's operating profit," the company said in its earnings report.

Globus reported an operating profit of 56.2 million forints for the first six months of 1997, compared to 113.5 million forints in the same period of 1996, and compared to its annual plan of 150 million forints.

Globus said its after-tax profit of 103.5 million forints, which remained below the after-tax profit of 111.6 million forints in the first six months of 1996, was in harmony with its annual target of 195 million forints.
The company's total net sales rose to 3.01 billion forints from last year's 2.37 billion forints.
Globus's exports rose faster than its domestic sales, as a result of which the proportion of domestic sales fell to 65 percent from 70 percent in the first half of 1996.
"The company boosted its positions on its export markets, primarily in the Commonwealth of Independent States and in the Baltic states," Globus said.
